indicator_definition: The consumer food price index measures changes over time in the prices paid by consumers for food and non-alcoholic beverages. It is expressed as an index with a reference period equal to 100. Rising food prices can increase food insecurity, particularly among lower-income households. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national statistical authorities.
rationale: Stable and affordable food prices are essential for ensuring access to adequate nutrition for all segments of the population. Sharp price increases disproportionately affect lower-income households and can push people into food insecurity. Monitoring this indicator contributes to the broader goal of ending hunger.
methodology_characteristics: Data are based on the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) food sub-index, collected monthly by national statistical authorities using standardised Eurostat methodology. The index covers all food and non-alcoholic beverages following the COICOP classification.
